messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 2-iodopyridine with 4-methylaniline; choose the ligand, base and isoxazole additive.

Variables and options:
ligand:
L1: tBuBrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C(C)(C)C)C(C)(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]
L2: tBuXPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C(C)(C)C)C(C)(C)C)C=CC=C2]
L3: XPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C=CC=C2]
L4: AdBrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P([C@@]3(C[C@@H]4C5)C[C@H](C4)C[C@H]5C3)[C@]6(C7)C[C@@H](C[C@@H]7C8)C[C@@H]8C6)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]

B1: BTMG [SMILES CC(C)(C)/N=C(N(C)C)/N(C)C]
B2: P2Et [SMILES CN(C)P(N(C)C)(N(C)C)=NP(N(C)C)(N(C)C)=NCC]
B3: MTBD [SMILES CN1CCCN2C1=NCCC2]

additive:
A1: 5-phenylisoxazole [SMILES C1(C2=CC=CC=C2)=CC=NO1]
A2: 4-phenylisoxazole [SMILES C1(C2=CC=CC=C2)=CON=C1]

A13: ethyl 3-methylisoxazole-5-carboxylate [SMILES CC1=NOC(C(OCC)=O)=C1]
A14: 3-methyl-5-phenylisoxazole [SMILES CC1=NOC(C2=CC=CC=C2)=C1]

A22: methyl 5-(thiophen-2-yl)isoxazole-3-carboxylate [SMILES O=C(OC)C1=NOC(C2=CC=CS2)=C1]

Experiments so far (best first):
L2 | B3 | A13 -> 99.6%
L4 | B3 | A14 -> 90.6%
L1 | B3 | A10 -> 89.3%

Propose exactly 15 NEW experiments not listed above. Return JSON:
{"picks": [{"ligand": "<label>", "base": "<label>", "additive": "<label>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}]}

picks.reason: This ester-bearing 3-methoxyisoxazole is a close structural probe of the top-performing A13 additive under the best observed ligand/base pair.
Testing this positional ester regioisomer can reveal whether the strong A13 result depends on its isoxazole substitution pattern.
This methyl/ester regioisomer provides a close comparison to A13 while retaining the potentially beneficial ester functionality.
The 5-carboxylate retains an ester-bearing isoxazole motif and tests whether the additional methyl substituent in A13 is important.
This unsubstituted isoxazole-3-carboxylate tests the value of A13's methyl substituent while preserving its ester group.
This ester-bearing regioisomer tests whether additive performance is sensitive to the carboxylate position.
A14 gave a strong result with L4, so testing it with the leading L2/B3 pair checks for a better ligand-additive match.
A10 performed well with L1, and this experiment tests whether its benefit transfers to the leading ligand.
This simple methylisoxazole tests whether a less substituted analogue can retain the benefit observed with A13.
A19 showed promising activity with L4, so combining it with the best observed ligand/base pair is a useful cross-comparison.
This phenylisoxazole regioisomer broadens the additive screen while holding the leading ligand and base fixed.
This directly tests whether the top additive remains highly effective with the ligand that previously gave a strong result with B3.
This compares the XPhos scaffold against the leading tBuXPhos condition while retaining the best additive and base.
This checks whether the strong A13 result transfers to AdBrettPhos, which has already shown good performance with B3.
This isolates the base effect with the best observed ligand/additive combination and compares phosphazene base B2 against B3.
